models_evaluated: Qwen3-32B general LLM with chain-of-thought prompting

links.outcome: Positive factual hallucination rate in refined HPI notes, RAG multi-agent model vs general LLM with CoT
links.effect: Hallucination rate 6.67% for HQ-ANR (knowledge-grounded RAG) vs 26.67% for general LLM with CoT; median PDQI-9 rose from 39.00 to 42.00.
links.quote: In a blinded evaluation of 30 resident-drafted hyperthyroidism notes, HQ-ANR significantly improved median Physician Documentation Quality Instrument (PDQI-9) scores (from 39.00 to 42.00) and reduced the hallucination rate (positive factual hallucinations only) to 6.67%, compared to 26.67% for a general LLM with chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting.

unlisted_practices: Multi-agent decomposition (separate agents for symptoms, examinations, treatments) to improve clinical note quality

screen.reason: The study develops and evaluates HQ-ANR (a multi-agent RAG system) against a baseline LLM to test whether knowledge grounding/RAG and multi-agent verification reduces hallucinations and improves clinical note quality.

primary.practice: retrieval-augmented generation and multi-agent guardrails for hallucination mitigation
